# What Trawl contacts

<!-- Generated by `go run ./cmd/egressdoc`. Do not edit by hand: this file is
     derived from the egress profiles the checks themselves declare, so that it
     cannot describe behaviour the code does not have. -->

Every DNS and email assessment check states, as structured data, what it
touches. This deployment's policy is expressed over those categories rather
than over check names, so a check added in a future release is admitted only
if everything it needs was already permitted. A check requiring anything else
is withheld and recorded as `not_checked`, with the reason below - it does not
run and then get reported, and it does not run quietly.

## Categories of contact

| Category | Meaning | Permitted here |
|---|---|---|
| `intrusive` | Contact beyond an ordinary query, such as requesting a zone transfer. Never destructive, but worth agreeing to. | no |
| `offline` | No network contact at all. | yes |
| `resolver` | Ordinary DNS queries through a recursive resolver. | yes |
| `target-https` | HTTPS requests to your own infrastructure, such as retrieving an MTA-STS policy file. | yes |
| `target-nameservers` | Queries sent straight to your domain's authoritative nameservers, which is visible to them in a way an ordinary query is not. | no |
| `third-party` | Contact with a service that is neither yours nor the target's. Requires per-service consent as well. | no |

## Third-party services

Consent is per service, not blanket. Permitting the `third-party` category
alone grants nothing: a service added upstream is a new disclosure of your
names to someone, and it waits for a decision.

| Service | Endpoints | Consented here |
|---|---|---|
| `aws-ip-ranges` | `ip-ranges.amazonaws.com` | no |
| `certspotter` | `api.certspotter.com` | no |
| `cloudflare-ip-ranges` | `www.cloudflare.com`, `api.cloudflare.com` | no |
| `crtsh` | `crt.sh` | no |
| `fastly-ip-ranges` | `api.fastly.com` | no |
| `gcp-ip-ranges` | `www.gstatic.com` | no |

## Checks that run

| Check | What it assesses | What it contacts |
|---|---|---|
| `bimi` | Brand Indicators for Message Identification (default._bimi). | `resolver` |
| `caa` | Certification Authority Authorisation: which CAs may issue. | `resolver` |
| `dkim` | DKIM signing keys, probed across the selectors used by common providers. | `resolver` |
| `dmarc` | DMARC policy: what receivers should do with unauthenticated mail. | `resolver` |
| `dnssec` | DNSSEC chain of trust: keys, parent delegation, algorithms, signature validity and denial of existence. | `resolver` |
| `mtasts` | MTA-STS: enforced TLS for inbound mail, including the policy file. | `resolver`, `target-https` |
| `mx` | Mail exchangers published by the domain, and their hygiene. | `resolver` |
| `nssec` | NSEC/NSEC3 denial-of-existence records. | `resolver` |
| `ptr` | Reverse DNS for the domain's addresses. | `resolver` |
| `spf` | Sender Policy Framework: which hosts may send mail as the domain. | `resolver` |
| `tlsrpt` | SMTP TLS Reporting: where receivers report failures to negotiate TLS with the domain's mail exchangers. | `resolver` |

## Checks withheld

Each of these is recorded against the asset as `not_checked` with the
reason given, so a coverage figure never counts them as assessed.

| Check | Why it is withheld |
|---|---|
| `axfr` | check "axfr" requires egress class "target-nameservers", which this deployment has not permitted |
| `ct` | check "ct" requires egress class "third-party", which this deployment has not permitted |
| `net` | check "net" requires egress class "third-party", which this deployment has not permitted |
| `ns` | check "ns" requires egress class "target-nameservers", which this deployment has not permitted |
| `tko` | check "tko" requires egress class "target-nameservers", which this deployment has not permitted |
| `wild` | check "wild" requires egress class "target-nameservers", which this deployment has not permitted |

## Hosts the transport will permit

Besides the domains you have authorised, the assessment transport refuses
every host not listed here. The list is derived from the checks that actually
run, so consenting to a service whose checks are withheld opens nothing.

_None. Only names within your authorised domains are contacted._
